if: an adjustment arises in the current period
it is necessitated by circumstances which, though related to prior periods, are DETERMINED in the current period
no error or omission in preparing the prior periods' financial statements is involved
then: it is NOT a prior period item
note: AS 5 gives the worked case: arrears payable to workers as a result of a retrospective wage revision during the current period. The prior statements were right when made; the obligation was created later. This is the rule that stops a bookkeeping system from labelling every backdated payment a prior period item.

evidence.quote: The term does not include other adjustments necessitated by circumstances, which though related to prior periods, are determined in the current period, e.g., arrears payable to workers as a result of revision of wages with retrospective effect during the current period.

as defined in this Statement, refers only to income or expenses which arise in the current period as a result of errors or omissions in the preparation of the financial statements of one or more prior periods.
